title: The Limit-Embracing Life
coreMove: A limit-embracing life starts when measured hours stop judging your worth; use calendars for coordination, then refuse demands that turn every moment into proof.

exampleSpecs.domain: operations planning after reading clock history
exampleSpecs.audience: workers who judge themselves by clean calendars
exampleSpecs.stakes: separate useful scheduling from moral self-audit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist uses Mumford's clock history to notice when hour blocks become containers of self-worth

exampleSpecs.domain: payroll meeting about factory time discipline
exampleSpecs.audience: managers tempted to treat every pause as waste
exampleSpecs.stakes: notice when hourly accounting turns attention into company property
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees Crowley's rules as a warning about treating nonwork minutes as stolen time

exampleSpecs.domain: startup metrics deck using industrial history
exampleSpecs.audience: analysts who confuse measurement with mastery
exampleSpecs.stakes: avoid selling efficiency as freedom from limits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist revises a metrics slide so clock coordination does not become a promise of total control

exampleSpecs.domain: postmortem after a productivity system collapse
exampleSpecs.audience: people who keep upgrading systems to escape anxiety
exampleSpecs.stakes: locate relief in surrendering impossible mastery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist interprets a Brooklyn productivity collapse as the end of the mastery fantasy

exampleSpecs.audience: professionals who turn every block into future payoff
exampleSpecs.stakes: stop treating present moments as auditions for a later life
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist connects Inbox Zero and Pomodoro habits to the habit of postponing life into a mastered future

exampleSpecs.domain: museum exhibit design about industrial time
exampleSpecs.audience: educators explaining time discipline without nostalgia
exampleSpecs.stakes: teach the hard edge without blaming clocks alone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist presents Crowley's ironworks as a social bargain, not proof that clocks themselves are evil
